newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine gov't asks Duhalde to explain remarks.
newsitem.headline: Argentine gov't asks Duhalde to explain remarks.

text.p: Argentine Cabinet Chief Jorge Rodrmguez said the leading contender to become the Peronist standard-bearer in national presidential elections should explain remarks he made that the opposition was not to blame for violence in last week's general strike, a newspaper reported Monday.
"If that is exactly what he said...I think he will have to explain," Rodrmguez said, quoted by the Clarmn newspaper.
Buenos Aires province Gov. Eduardo Duhalde said on the weekend that he did not think that the opposition Alliance was to blame for the violence that broke out during last Thursday's general strike.
Duhalde's comments contradicted those of President Carlos Menem, who said that Alliance members bore intellectual responsibility for the clashes.
Duhalde is seen by analysts as the leading contender to be the Peronist candidate in the 1999 presidential elections, in which Menem is constitutionally prohibited from competing.
But, with mid-term congressional elections approaching in October, tensions between Duhalde and Menem have already surfaced several times this year.

The general strike was called by unions opposed to the government. The recently-formed Alliance between the Frepaso and Radical parties said it sympathized with the strikers, but not with the form of protest taken.
Scores of demonstrators were arrested during the strike, which was marked by several violent clashes between small groups of protestors manning roadblocks and police.
Opposition politicians denied any responsibility for the incidents and accused Menem of trying to score political points.
The government said that about a quarter of workers participated in the strike -- which was boycotted by Peronist unions -- but strike leaders claimed to have brought the country to a halt.
